questions.question: What is the name of the earliest form of writing known in the Indian subcontinent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indus Script**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indus Script** is the earliest form of writing known in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It was used by the Indus Valley Civilization, which flourished around 2600 to 1900 BCE in what is now Pakistan and northwest India.
 
• The script is found on various artifacts, including seals, pottery, and tablets.
 
• Despite numerous attempts, the Indus Script remains undeciphered, and its exact nature and function are still subjects of research and debate.
 
• It consists of numerous symbols, some of which are repeated frequently, suggesting a complex system of writing or proto-writing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indus Valley Civilization** is one of the world's oldest urban civilizations, along with Mesopotamia and Ancient Egypt.
 
• The major sites of this civilization include Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, and Lothal.
 
• The civilization is noted for its advanced urban planning, architecture, and social organization.
 
• The discovery of the Indus Script has provided valuable insights into the culture and practices of the Indus Valley people, despite its undeciphered state.
 
• Efforts to decode the script involve comparative analysis with other ancient scripts and languages, but no definitive translation has been achieved so far.

questions.question: According to the Women's Reservation Bill, 2023, how many seats in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies are reserved for women?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one-third**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **One-third** of the seats in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies are reserved for women according to the Women's Reservation Bill, 2023.
 
• The bill aims to enhance women's representation in legislative bodies, promoting gender equality in political participation.
 
• This reservation will be applicable for a period of 15 years from the commencement of the act.
 
• The seats reserved for women will be rotated after every general election to ensure a fair representation across different constituencies.
 
• This initiative is seen as a significant step towards empowering women and ensuring their active involvement in the legislative process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Women's Reservation Bill was first introduced in 1996 and has seen several revisions before its passage in 2023.
 
• India has a history of women leaders in politics, including Indira Gandhi, the first female Prime Minister, and Pratibha Patil, the first female President.
 
• Women's representation in local governance has been mandated since the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, which reserve one-third of seats in Panchayats and Municipalities for women.
 
• The bill is expected to pave the way for more women to take on leadership roles and influence policy-making at the national and state levels.
 
• Globally, several countries have implemented similar reservations or quotas to boost women's representation in politics.

questions.question: Pandit Birju Maharaj was an Indian dancer, composer, singer, and exponent of the __________ "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana of Kathak dance in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lucknow**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Birju Maharaj** was an Indian dancer, composer, singer, and exponent of the "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana of Kathak dance in India.
 
• The "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana is associated with the **Lucknow** style of Kathak dance.
 
• Birju Maharaj was renowned for his mastery in Kathak and contributed significantly to its popularization both in India and internationally.
 
• He received several prestigious awards, including the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• The word "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word "Katha," meaning story, and "Kathakar," meaning the one who tells a story.
 
• The dance form traces its origins to the ancient North Indian temples where the Kathakars, or storytellers, used to narrate stories from epics and mythology through dance and music.
 
• The Lucknow Gharana of Kathak emphasizes graceful movements, intricate footwork, and expressive facial gestures.
 
• Pandit Birju Maharaj was instrumental in choreographing dance sequences for several Bollywood films, bringing Kathak to a wider audience.

questions.question: Which institution was established in 2015, in the place of Planning commission of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **NITI Aayog** was established in 2015, replacing the Planning Commission of India.
 
• NITI Aayog stands for **National Institution for Transforming India**.
 
• It was formed to promote cooperative federalism and to foster involvement and participation of the state governments in the economic policy-making process using a bottom-up approach.
 
• The institution serves as a policy think tank for the Indian government and provides strategic and technical advice on a range of issues including economic policy and development priorities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Planning Commission of India was established in **1950** and was responsible for formulating India’s Five-Year Plans.
 
• The primary objective of the Planning Commission was to ensure the balanced and effective allocation of resources and to promote economic development.
 
• With the establishment of NITI Aayog, the focus shifted from a centralized planning approach to a more decentralized and inclusive model of development.
 
• NITI Aayog is headed by the **Prime Minister of India** and comprises a governing council with Chief Ministers of all the states and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Satyashodhak Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyotirao Phule**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jyotirao Phule** was the founder of the Satyashodhak Samaj.
 
• Satyashodhak Samaj, also known as the "Truth Seekers' Society," was established in **1873** in Maharashtra.
 
• The main objective of the organization was to promote social equality and fight against the caste system and other social injustices prevalent in society.
 
• Jyotirao Phule was a prominent social reformer and thinker who worked tirelessly for the upliftment of the oppressed and marginalized sections of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Jyotirao Phule** was also instrumental in promoting education for women and the lower castes.
 
• He, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, established the first school for girls in Pune in **1848**.
 
• Phule's writings and activism played a crucial role in the social and educational reform movements in India during the 19th century.
 
• His notable works include "Gulamgiri" (Slavery) and "Shetkarayacha Asud" (Cultivator's Whipcord).

questions.question: When Mendeleev started his work, how many elements were known at that time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**63**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **63 elements** were known when Mendeleev started his work on the periodic table.
 
• Mendeleev's periodic table was revolutionary because he organized the elements based on their atomic mass and predicted the existence and properties of new elements.
 
• His periodic table allowed for the prediction of the properties of elements that had not yet been discovered.
 
• Mendeleev's work laid the groundwork for the modern periodic table, which is based on atomic number rather than atomic mass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev** was a Russian chemist who is best known for creating the Periodic Table of Elements.
 
• He arranged the 63 known elements into a table based on atomic mass, which revealed that elements with similar properties occurred at regular intervals.
 
• Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table for elements that were not yet discovered, confidently predicting their properties and atomic masses.
 
• These gaps were later filled with the discovery of elements such as gallium and germanium, which confirmed the accuracy and utility of Mendeleev's periodic table.
 
• The modern periodic table is arranged by increasing atomic number, which is the number of protons in an atom's nucleus, rather than atomic mass.
 
• Mendeleev's periodic law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic masses.

questions.question:
Complete the statement given below with respect to the judge's removal.

The Indian Constitution :-

options.text: prescribes a procedure for removal of high court judges only.
prescribes a very difficult procedure for removal of judges.
does not prescribe a procedure for removal of judges.
prescribes a very flexible procedure for removal of judges.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**prescribes a very difficult procedure for removal of judges**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Constitution **prescribes a very difficult procedure for removal of judges**.
 
• The process for removal of judges is outlined in **Article 124(4) and Article 217(1)(b)** of the Constitution.
 
• The removal process involves a motion being passed by a special majority in both houses of Parliament on grounds of proven misbehavior or incapacity.
 
• This stringent procedure ensures judicial independence and protects judges from arbitrary removal.
 
• The process is designed to be exhaustive to maintain the integrity and impartiality of the judiciary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The removal of a judge is a rare and serious event, reflecting the high standards of accountability for the judiciary in India.
 
• The procedure for removal of judges is a critical component of the checks and balances within the Indian democratic framework.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding badminton?

I. At the beginning of the game of badminton and when the score is even, the server serves from the left service court.

II. Server and receiver always stand in opposite service courts but on the same side.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4 Neither I nor II**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Statement I:** At the beginning of the game of badminton and when the score is even, the server serves from the left service court.

 
 
• This statement is incorrect. In badminton, the server serves from the right service court when the score is even and from the left service court when the score is odd.
 
 
 
• **Statement II:** Server and receiver always stand in opposite service courts but on the same side.
 
 
• This statement is also incorrect. The server and receiver stand in diagonally opposite service courts, not on the same side.
 
 

Therefore, neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct.
